title: Monetary Dark Matter: Constitutive Labor, Obligating Provenance, and the Shear into Money-Form
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A theoretical paper on monetary shear after semantic constitution: monetary dark matter, obligating provenance, productive provenance shear, the referential register of money, and the distinct exposure law of the Baal counter-transition. Version 0.2 also restores the first-edition Marxian Form IV as an analytical instrument and separates circulating carrier stock from accumulated exposure in the transition bridge.
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate) — drafted in working session with Claude (Anthropic) under MANUS direction; the v0.2 mathematical repair to §§8.3, 25.2, 25.4 and Appendix A was conducted in ChatGPT (OpenAI) under MANUS direction before deposit.
methodology: The paper develops a formal distinction between constitutive semantic labor and monetary shear, tests the distinction against the monetary body's material and referential registers, reconstructs the relevant first-edition Marxian value-form sequence from the cited MEGA² volumes, and states observed, inferred, and untested claims separately. The transition appendix rotates the existing latency/activation model into a heterogeneous counter-transition model. Before deposit, the exposure dynamics were repaired so withdrawal acts on circulating carrier stock and future exposure production rather than erasing already accumulated exposure.
falsification_conditions: The stronger claims would be weakened if matched controls show that inscription does not produce a measurable singular premium or differential withdrawal; if reactivating obligating provenance does not alter permissions, distribution, attribution, ownership, liability, settlement, or standing where the theory predicts it should; if the proposed productive shear cannot be distinguished from ordinary transmission-cost compression; or if the particular/universal inscription regimes do not differ once carrier stock, exposure, and secondary propagation are measured separately.
axn_reading: Closure -> Play -> Text -> Duration -> Play -> Foundation
wiki_article: Monetary Dark Matter is a theoretical paper in the Semantic Economy sequence. It argues that money can enter a field only after constitutive labor has already made that field identifiable, related, transmissible, and provenance-bearing, and that monetary operation may then shear away relations that remain causally load-bearing. The paper distinguishes monetary dark matter from mere missing information and defines productive provenance shear for cases in which a relation's loss of operative standing increases monetary capacity. Its monetary-body specimen separates denomination from a second singular price, while its provenance analysis distinguishes authorizing from obligating relations. Version 0.2 also develops the transition bridge: standing is factored into latency and activation, reassimilation is modeled as descriptive retention without operative force, and the Baal counter-transition is given a distinct exposure law in which circulating carrier stock, cumulative exposure, latent power, and activation are separate state variables. The appendix leaves the counter-transition formally incomplete where monetary grammar, carrier identity, and substrate writeability remain to be operationalized.
